claim: Human cytomegalovirus (hCMV) immediate early 1 (IE1) protein associates with condensed chromatin of the host cell during mitosis.
source: Human cytomegalovirus (hCMV) immediate early 1 (IE1) protein associates with condensed chromatin of the host cell during mitosis.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations in the manuscript text.

claim: The structure of the chromatin-tethering domain (CTD) of IE1 bound to the nucleosome core particle has been determined at 2.8 Å resolution.
source: The complex of NCP with an IE1-CTD peptide (a.a. 476–491) was obtained by soaking the peptide into preformed NCP crystals, and a 2.8 Å structure was solved by molecular replacement.
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental determination of the crystal structure.

claim: The specific interaction between IE1-CTD and the H2A-H2B acidic patch impairs the compaction of higher-order chromatin structure.
source: We have determined the structure of the chromatin-tethering domain (CTD) of IE1 bound to the nucleosome core particle, and discovered that the specific interaction between IE1-CTD and the H2A-H2B acidic patch impairs the compaction of higher-order chromatin structure.
evidence: This claim is supported by structural and functional data presented in the manuscript.

claim: IE1 loosens up the folding of host chromatin during hCMV infections.
source: Our results suggest that IE1 loosens up the folding of host chromatin during hCMV infections.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented in the manuscript.

claim: The nucleosome typically assembles 146–147 bp of DNA wrapped around a histone octamer consisting of two copies each of H3, H4, H2A and H2B.
source: The nucleosome, the basic repeating unit of chromatin, typically assembles 146–147 bp of DNA wrapped around a histone octamer consisting of two copies each of H3, H4, H2A and H2B (Luger et al., 1997a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The interaction between the N-terminal tail of histone H4 and the acidic patch plays crucial roles for the formation of 30-nm chromatin fiber.
source: The interaction between the N-terminal tail of histone H4 and a specific surface region on the neighboring nucleosome termed the"acidic patch" plays crucial roles for the formation of 30-nm chromatin fiber (Dorigo et al., 2004; Luger et al., 1997a; Song et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The acidic patch is formed by negatively charged residues including Glu56, Glu61, Glu64, Asp90, Glu91 and Glu92 of H2A, and Glu102 and Glu110 of H2B.
source: The acidic patch is formed by a number of negatively charged residues of H2A and H2B, including Glu56, Glu61, Glu64, Asp90, Glu91 and Glu92 of H2A, and Glu102 and Glu110 of H2B (Luger et al., 1997a).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Several nucleosome-binding proteins specifically interact with the acidic patch.
source: Several nucleosome-binding proteins have been shown to specifically interact with the acidic patch.
evidence: This is supported by the broader scientific literature context.

claim: Proteins that bind the acidic patch may regulate higher-order chromatin structure by competing with the H4 N-terminal tails.
source: Therefore, it has been hypothesized that these proteins may play a role in regulating the higher-order chromatin structure by competing with the H4 N-terminal tails for binding to the acidic patch of the nucleosome (Kalashnikova et al., 2013; McGinty and Tan, 2015).
evidence: This is a hypothesis supported by citations.

claim: The 72-kDa IE1 protein of hCMV plays critical roles in viral early gene expression and DNA replication.
source: The 72-kDa immediately early 1 (IE1) protein of human cytomegalovirus (hCMV) plays critical roles in the viral early gene expression and DNA replication (Gawn and Greaves, 2002; Mocarski et al., 1996).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: IE1 has been long known to associate with condensed host chromatin during mitosis.
source: In addition, IE1 has been long known to associate with condensed host chromatin during mitosis (Ahn et al., 1998; Dimitropoulou et al., 2010; Huh et al., 2008; Krauss et al., 2009; Lafemina et al., 1989; Nevels et al., 2004; Reinhardt et al., 2005; Shin et al., 2012; Wilkinson et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by extensive citations to previous research.

claim: The chromatin-tethering domain (CTD) located at the very C-terminal end of IE1 (a.a 476–491) is responsible for the association with the mitotic chromosome.
source: The chromatin-tethering domain (CTD) located at the very C-terminal end of IE1 (a.a 476–491) is responsible for the association with the mitotic chromosome, specifically through the acidic patch of the nucleosome (Mucke et al., 2014; Reinhardt et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: IE1-CTD associates with the mitotic chromosome specifically through the acidic patch of the nucleosome.
source: The chromatin-tethering domain (CTD) located at the very C-terminal end of IE1 (a.a 476–491) is responsible for the association with the mitotic chromosome, specifically through the acidic patch of the nucleosome (Mucke et al., 2014; Reinhardt et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The structure shows one molecule of IE1-CTD bound to the NCP.
source: The structure shows one molecule of IE1-CTD bound to the NCP (Figure 1A; Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure and shown in figures.

claim: The presence of only one IE1-CTD peptide in the complex structure is due to the availability of only one side of the NCP surface in the preformed crystal lattice.
source: The presence of only one IE1-CTD peptide in the complex structure is due to the availability of only one side of the NCP surface in the preformed crystal lattice, as in the case of NCP in complex with the latency-associated antigen (LANA) of Kaposi's sarcoma-associated herpes virus (KSHV) (Barbera et al., 2006).
evidence: This is an inference based on crystallographic constraints and comparison to a similar case.

claim: The IE1-CTD peptide adopts an extended, v-shaped conformation with a short α-helix at its C-terminus.
source: The IE1-CTD peptide adopts an extended, v-shaped conformation with a short α-helix at its C-terminus.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: IE1-CTD is well positioned into the acidic patch of the nucleosome formed by H2A and H2B.
source: In the complex structure, IE1-CTD is well positioned into the acidic patch of the nucleosome formed by H2A and H2B (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure and shown in figures.

claim: IE1-CTD contacts histone H2B at two distinct sites through van der Waals interaction and intermolecular hydrogen bonds via its mainchain groups.
source: IE1-CTD contacts histone H2B at two distinct sites, the C-terminal portion of α1 and the N-terminal half of αC, through van der Waals interaction and intermolecular hydrogen bonds via its mainchain groups.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The amide and carbonyl groups of Thr480 make hydrogen bonds with the mainchain carbonyl and the sidechain amide groups of Gln44 of H2B.
source: Specifically, the amide and carbonyl groups of Thr480 make hydrogen bonds with the mainchain carbonyl and the sidechain amide groups of Gln44 of H2B (amino acid residue numbering following that in the reference of Luger et al., 1997a); the amide and carbonyl groups of Val484 bond the carboxylate group of Glu110 and the nitrogen atom of the imidazole ring of His106, respectively (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The amide and carbonyl groups of Val484 bond the carboxylate group of Glu110 and the nitrogen atom of the imidazole ring of His106.
source: Specifically, the amide and carbonyl groups of Thr480 make hydrogen bonds with the mainchain carbonyl and the sidechain amide groups of Gln44 of H2B (amino acid residue numbering following that in the reference of Luger et al., 1997a); the amide and carbonyl groups of Val484 bond the carboxylate group of Glu110 and the nitrogen atom of the imidazole ring of His106, respectively (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: His481 makes one hydrogen bond with Glu56 of H2A.
source: His481 makes one hydrogen bond with Glu56 of H2A; Thr485 and Ser487 each makes one hydrogen bond with Glu64 of H2A; and Arg486 makes hydrogen bonds with Glu61 on α2, as well as with Asp90 and Glu92 located on αC of histone H2A.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Thr485 and Ser487 each makes one hydrogen bond with Glu64 of H2A.
source: His481 makes one hydrogen bond with Glu56 of H2A; Thr485 and Ser487 each makes one hydrogen bond with Glu64 of H2A; and Arg486 makes hydrogen bonds with Glu61 on α2, as well as with Asp90 and Glu92 located on αC of histone H2A.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Arg486 makes hydrogen bonds with Glu61 on α2, as well as with Asp90 and Glu92 located on αC of histone H2A.
source: His481 makes one hydrogen bond with Glu56 of H2A; Thr485 and Ser487 each makes one hydrogen bond with Glu64 of H2A; and Arg486 makes hydrogen bonds with Glu61 on α2, as well as with Asp90 and Glu92 located on αC of histone H2A.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Met483 of IE1-CTD is placed in a hydrophobic pocket consisting of Leu23, and the aliphatic portion of Glu56 and Tyr57.
source: In addition, Met483 of IE1-CTD is placed in a hydrophobic pocket consisting of Leu23, and the aliphatic portion of Glu56 and Tyr57.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The nucleosomal acidic patch is well known for hosting the binding of a number of proteins.
source: The nucleosomal acidic patch is well known for hosting the binding of a number of proteins (Armache et al., 2011; Arnaudo et al., 2013; Barbera et al., 2006; Kato et al., 2013; Makde et al., 2010; McGinty et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: hCMV IE1 is most closely related to LANA of KSHV among acidic patch-binding proteins.
source: Most closely related to hCMV IE1 is LANA of KSHV (Barbera et al., 2006).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison and supported by citation.

claim: The N-terminal CTD of LANA forms a hairpin-like structure that pokes into the acidic patch of the nucleosome.
source: The N-terminal CTD of LANA forms a hairpin-like structure that pokes into the acidic patch of the nucleosome (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on the known structure of LANA-NCP complex.

claim: Three IE1-CTD residues (Met483, Arg486 and Ser487) occupy the same regions of the acidic patch and engage the same sets of histone residues as the corresponding LANA residues.
source: Structural comparison reveals that three IE1-CTD residues, Met483, Arg486 and Ser487, occupy the same regions of the acidic patch and engage the same sets of histone residues as the corresponding LANA residues in binding the nucleosome (Figure 1C, D, 2A and B).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison between IE1-CTD and LANA complexes.

claim: Arg486 interacts with the acidic patch in a manner commonly found in the structures of protein-nucleosome complexes known to date.
source: In particular, Arg486 interacts with the acidic patch in a manner commonly found in the structures of protein-nucleosome complexes known to date (Figure 2A–F).
evidence: This is based on comparison with multiple protein-NCP complex structures.

claim: The acidic patch can be divided into three adjoining ligand-binding zones.
source: A careful examination of the acidic patch reveals that it can be divided into three adjoining ligand-binding zones (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an analysis and classification based on structural examination.

claim: Zone I is formed by Glu61, Leu65, Asp90 and Glu92 of histone H2A, and Glu102 and Leu103 of histone H2B.
source: Zone I is formed by Glu61, Leu65, Asp90 and Glu92 of histone H2A, and Glu102 and Leu103 of histone H2B; Zone II is formed by histone H2A residues Tyr57, Ala60, Glu61 and Glu64, and the latter serves as a ridge separating zone I and II; and zone III is formed by Glu56 and Ala60 of H2A, and Val41, Gln44 and Glu110 of histone H2B.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the acidic patch.

claim: Zone II is formed by histone H2A residues Tyr57, Ala60, Glu61 and Glu64, with Glu64 serving as a ridge separating zone I and II.
source: Zone I is formed by Glu61, Leu65, Asp90 and Glu92 of histone H2A, and Glu102 and Leu103 of histone H2B; Zone II is formed by histone H2A residues Tyr57, Ala60, Glu61 and Glu64, and the latter serves as a ridge separating zone I and II; and zone III is formed by Glu56 and Ala60 of H2A, and Val41, Gln44 and Glu110 of histone H2B.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the acidic patch.

claim: Zone III is formed by Glu56 and Ala60 of H2A, and Val41, Gln44 and Glu110 of histone H2B.
source: Zone I is formed by Glu61, Leu65, Asp90 and Glu92 of histone H2A, and Glu102 and Leu103 of histone H2B; Zone II is formed by histone H2A residues Tyr57, Ala60, Glu61 and Glu64, and the latter serves as a ridge separating zone I and II; and zone III is formed by Glu56 and Ala60 of H2A, and Val41, Gln44 and Glu110 of histone H2B.
evidence: This is based on structural analysis of the acidic patch.

claim: The binding of an arginine in zone I is conserved among all protein-NCP complexes known thus far.
source: The binding of an arginine in zone I is conserved among all protein-NCP complexes known thus far.
evidence: This is based on comparison of multiple protein-NCP complex structures.

claim: Thr485 of IE1 and Leu8 of LANA are bound in zone II, which is unoccupied in other NCP complexes.
source: Thr485 of IE1 and Leu8 of LANA are bound in zone II, which is unoccupied in other NCP complexes (Figure 2).
evidence: This is based on comparison of multiple protein-NCP complex structures.

claim: His481 of IE1-CTD is bound in zone III and makes a hydrogen bond with Glu56 of H2A.
source: Main differences accounting for the specific interaction between IE1-CTD and NCP appear to reside in His481, which is bound in zone III and makes a hydrogen bond with Glu56 of H2A, and Thr485, which is bound to zone II and forms a hydrogen bond with Glu64 of H2A.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Thr485 of IE1-CTD is bound to zone II and forms a hydrogen bond with Glu64 of H2A.
source: Main differences accounting for the specific interaction between IE1-CTD and NCP appear to reside in His481, which is bound in zone III and makes a hydrogen bond with Glu56 of H2A, and Thr485, which is bound to zone II and forms a hydrogen bond with Glu64 of H2A.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: The binding of the N-terminal segment of IE1-CTD spanning residues 476–480 to α1 of H2B is unique to IE1.
source: And finally, the binding of the N-terminal segment of IE1-CTD spanning residues 476–480 to α1 of H2B is unique to IE1 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on comparison with other protein-NCP complexes.

claim: Wild-type IE1-CTD bound to recombinant human NCP with a dissociation constant (KD) of 0.4 μM.
source: Wild-type IE1-CTD bound to recombinant human NCP with a dissociation constant (KD) of 0.4 μM, while its mutant lacking the N-terminal segment interacting with α1 of H2B (Δ476–480) reduced the nucleosome-binding affinity to a KD of 12 μM (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: The IE1-CTD mutant lacking the N-terminal segment (Δ476–480) reduced the nucleosome-binding affinity to a KD of 12 μM.
source: Wild-type IE1-CTD bound to recombinant human NCP with a dissociation constant (KD) of 0.4 μM, while its mutant lacking the N-terminal segment interacting with α1 of H2B (Δ476–480) reduced the nucleosome-binding affinity to a KD of 12 μM (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: Full-length IE1 binds approximately five-fold weaker than IE1-CTD alone to NCP.
source: To put the binding affinities in perspective, an approximately five-fold weaker binding of full-length IE1 than IE1-CTD alone to NCP was observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), possibly caused by self-inhibitory effects of other domains in the full-length protein.
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: The weaker binding of full-length IE1 compared to IE1-CTD is possibly caused by self-inhibitory effects of other domains in the full-length protein.
source: To put the binding affinities in perspective, an approximately five-fold weaker binding of full-length IE1 than IE1-CTD alone to NCP was observed (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B), possibly caused by self-inhibitory effects of other domains in the full-length protein.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed data.

claim: IE1 lacking the CTD showed no detectable binding to NCP.
source: In comparison, IE1 lacking the CTD showed no detectable binding to NCP (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: The H481A mutant of IE1-CTD has a KD of 43.4 μM, representing the most severe reduction of binding affinity.
source: With IE1-CTD, the most severe reduction of binding affinity was seen in the H481A mutant, which has a KD of 43.4 μM (Figure 3C), while loss of one hydrogen bond by substituting Thr485 with a valine brought the KD to 11.3 μM (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: The T485V mutant of IE1-CTD has a KD of 11.3 μM.
source: With IE1-CTD, the most severe reduction of binding affinity was seen in the H481A mutant, which has a KD of 43.4 μM (Figure 3C), while loss of one hydrogen bond by substituting Thr485 with a valine brought the KD to 11.3 μM (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: The NCP reconstituted with the E56R mutant of H2A lowered the binding to IE1-CTD to a level beyond detection.
source: ITC measurement shows that the NCP reconstituted with the E56R mutant of H2A, a charge-swap mutant, lowered the binding to IE1-CTD to a level beyond detection (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: The H2A E56R mutation reduced the binding of LANA to NCP from a KD of 0.25 to 23.4 μM.
source: This change of histone H2A also brought about a conspicuous reduction of the binding of LANA to NCP from a KD of 0.25 to 23.4 μM (Figure 3F and G).
evidence: This is measured by ITC experiments.

claim: LANA and IE1 share the methionine-mediated interaction with Glu56 in zone III of the acidic patch.
source: LANA and IE1 share the methionine-mediated interaction with Glu56 in zone III of the acidic patch (Figure 2A and B), and the greater compromise of the binding of IE1-CTD to the H2A-E56R NCP reflects the importance of the His481-Glu56 hydrogen bond in the IE1-NCP complex, as compared to the van der Waals interaction between Thr14 of LANA and Glu56 of histone H2A (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is based on structural comparison.

claim: The greater compromise of IE1-CTD binding to H2A-E56R NCP reflects the importance of the His481-Glu56 hydrogen bond compared to the van der Waals interaction between Thr14 of LANA and Glu56.
source: LANA and IE1 share the methionine-mediated interaction with Glu56 in zone III of the acidic patch (Figure 2A and B), and the greater compromise of the binding of IE1-CTD to the H2A-E56R NCP reflects the importance of the His481-Glu56 hydrogen bond in the IE1-NCP complex, as compared to the van der Waals interaction between Thr14 of LANA and Glu56 of histone H2A (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of the E56R mutation on IE1 and LANA binding.

claim: The τ nitrogen of the imidazole ring of His481 makes a hydrogen bond with the carboxylate group of Glu56 of histone H2A at a distance of approximately 2.9 Å.
source: These two residues interact with Glu56 of histone H2A differently in the structure: while the τ nitrogen of the imidazole ring of His481 makes a hydrogen bond with the carboxylate group of Glu56 of histone H2A at a distance of approximately 2.9 Å, Thr14 of LANA contacts Glu56 of H2A approximately 5 Å away via van der Waals interaction.
evidence: This is directly observed in the crystal structure.

claim: Thr14 of LANA contacts Glu56 of H2A approximately 5 Å away via van der Waals interaction.
source: These two residues interact with Glu56 of histone H2A differently in the structure: while the τ nitrogen of the imidazole ring of His481 makes a hydrogen bond with the carboxylate group of Glu56 of histone H2A at a distance of approximately 2.9 Å, Thr14 of LANA contacts Glu56 of H2A approximately 5 Å away via van der Waals interaction.
evidence: This is based on the known LANA-NCP structure.

claim: In the absence of IE1-CTD, the nucleosomal array sedimented with a median sedimentation coefficient of 36 ± 1 S.
source: AUC experiments showed that, in the absence of IE1-CTD, the nucleosomal array sedimented with a median sedimentation coefficient Save (sedimentation coefficient at 50% boundary fraction) of 36 ± 1 S, and the 30-nm chromatin fiber sedimented at 51.5 ± 0.6 S (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: In the absence of IE1-CTD, the 30-nm chromatin fiber sedimented at 51.5 ± 0.6 S.
source: AUC experiments showed that, in the absence of IE1-CTD, the nucleosomal array sedimented with a median sedimentation coefficient Save (sedimentation coefficient at 50% boundary fraction) of 36 ± 1 S, and the 30-nm chromatin fiber sedimented at 51.5 ± 0.6 S (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: In the presence of IE1-CTD, the 10-nm nucleosomal array was unaffected.
source: In the presence of IE1-CTD, the 10-nm nucleosomal array was unaffected while Save of the 30-nm chromatin fiber shifted from 51.5 to 48 S, indicating that the binding of IE1-CTD made the chromatin fiber more loosely folded (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: In the presence of IE1-CTD, the Save of the 30-nm chromatin fiber shifted from 51.5 to 48 S.
source: In the presence of IE1-CTD, the 10-nm nucleosomal array was unaffected while Save of the 30-nm chromatin fiber shifted from 51.5 to 48 S, indicating that the binding of IE1-CTD made the chromatin fiber more loosely folded (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: The binding of IE1-CTD made the chromatin fiber more loosely folded.
source: In the presence of IE1-CTD, the 10-nm nucleosomal array was unaffected while Save of the 30-nm chromatin fiber shifted from 51.5 to 48 S, indicating that the binding of IE1-CTD made the chromatin fiber more loosely folded (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is an inference based on the AUC data showing reduced sedimentation coefficient.

claim: The IE1-CTD-containing chromatin fiber represents an altered chromatin state different from both the extended 10-nm nucleosomal array and the folded 30-nm chromatin fiber.
source: It should be emphasized that the IE1-CTD-containing chromatin fiber represents an altered chromatin state different from both the extended 10-nm nucleosomal array and the folded 30-nm chromatin fiber.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the AUC data.

claim: The chromatin-alteration property of IE1-CTD is shared by the full-length IE1.
source: This chromatin-alteration property of IE1-CTD is shared by the full-length IE1 and fully depends on the presence of CTD (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: The chromatin-alteration property of IE1 fully depends on the presence of CTD.
source: This chromatin-alteration property of IE1-CTD is shared by the full-length IE1 and fully depends on the presence of CTD (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments showing IE1ΔCTD has no effect.

claim: IE1-CTD mutants essentially retained the ability to decondense the 30-nm chromatin fiber.
source: Further AUC analyses with IE1-CTD mutants showed that they essentially retained the ability to decondense the 30-nm chromatin fiber, possibly due to their incomplete loss of NCP-binding abilities (Figure 4D, E and F).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: The retention of chromatin-altering ability by IE1-CTD mutants is possibly due to their incomplete loss of NCP-binding abilities.
source: Further AUC analyses with IE1-CTD mutants showed that they essentially retained the ability to decondense the 30-nm chromatin fiber, possibly due to their incomplete loss of NCP-binding abilities (Figure 4D, E and F).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed data.

claim: Chromatin fibers reconstituted with the E56R mutant of histone H2A displayed no alteration of chromatin folding by IE1-CTD.
source: By contrast, chromatin fibers reconstituted with the E56R mutant of histone H2A, previously shown to be unable to interact with IE1-CTD, displayed no alteration of chromatin folding by IE1-CTD (Figure 4G).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: The binding of IE1-CTD at the acidic patch of the nucleosome modulates the higher-order structure of chromatin.
source: These observations indicate that the binding of IE1-CTD at the acidic patch of the nucleosome modulates the higher-order structure of chromatin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the AUC experiments.

claim: Not all acidic patch-binding proteins affect chromatin folding.
source: It should be pointed out that not all acidic patch-binding proteins affect chromatin folding, as LANA does not alter the folding of 30-nm chromatin fiber in our AUC analysis (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: LANA does not alter the folding of 30-nm chromatin fiber.
source: It should be pointed out that not all acidic patch-binding proteins affect chromatin folding, as LANA does not alter the folding of 30-nm chromatin fiber in our AUC analysis (Figure 4H).
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: The LANA peptide promotes the compaction of nucleosomal arrays when folding is induced by magnesium ions.
source: It was shown previously that the LANA peptide promotes the compaction of nucleosomal arrays, judged by an assay in which the folding of nucleosomal arrays was induced by magnesium ions (Chodaparambil et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on a previous study cited in the manuscript.

claim: The addition of LANA made the nucleosomal arrays sediment slower.
source: In qualitative agreement with the previous observation, we saw that the addition of LANA made the nucleosomal arrays sedimented slower.
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments in the current study.

claim: Unlike IE1-CTD, LANA has no effect on the preformed H1-containing 30-nm chromatin fiber.
source: Nevertheless, unlike IE1-CTD, LANA has no effect on the preformed H1-containing 30-nm chromatin fiber.
evidence: This is measured by AUC experiments.

claim: IE1 and LANA differ in their ability to affect the folding of 30-nm chromatin fiber.
source: In either case, IE1 and LANA differ in their ability to affect the folding of 30-nm chromatin fiber.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the AUC experiments comparing IE1 and LANA.

claim: Distinct modes of protein binding to the acidic patch of the nucleosome could exert differential influences to chromatin folding.
source: The contrasting properties of IE1 and LANA suggest that distinct modes of protein binding to the acidic patch of the nucleosome could exert differential influences to chromatin folding.
evidence: This is a general conclusion inferred from the comparison of IE1 and LANA.

claim: The discovery of the chromatin modulating activity of IE1 should facilitate further mechanistic understanding of its functions in viral pathogenesis.
source: The discovery of the chromatin modulating activity of IE1 should facilitate further mechanistic understanding of its functions in viral pathogenesis, particularly its impact on the chromatin structure of the host genome, such as transcriptional regulation.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research implications.

claim: The most promising sites for isolating histone mutants that affect the binding of one protein but not others appear to lie in zone II and III of the acidic patch.
source: The most promising such sites appear to lie in zone II and III, as they are less frequently occupied among known NCP binding proteins (Figure 2).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural analysis of multiple protein-NCP complexes.

claim: Zone II and III are less frequently occupied among known NCP binding proteins.
source: The most promising such sites appear to lie in zone II and III, as they are less frequently occupied among known NCP binding proteins (Figure 2).
evidence: This is based on comparison of multiple protein-NCP complex structures.

claim: The E56R variant of histone H2A is an IE1-noninteracting mutant.
source: Nevertheless, the identification of the E56R variant of histone H2A as an IE1-noninteracting mutant has already served as a useful tool for assessing IE1's ability to modulate the higher-order structure of chromatin.
evidence: This is based on the ITC and AUC experiments showing loss of IE1 binding and chromatin alteration.

claim: The coordinates and diffraction data have been deposited in PDB under the accession code 5E5A.
source: The coordinates and diffraction data have been deposited in PDB under the accession code 5E5A.
evidence: This is a statement of data deposition.

claim: The Rwork and Rfree of the final model were 19.5% and 24.4%, respectively.
source: The Rwork and Rfree of the final model were 19.5% and 24.4%, respectively.
evidence: These are crystallographic refinement statistics.

claim: The structure was solved at a resolution of 2.80 Å.
evidence: This is stated in the crystallographic data collection statistics table.

claim: The space group of the crystal is P212121.
source: space group	P212121
evidence: This is stated in the crystallographic data collection statistics table.

claim: N-terminal tails of histone H4 are involved in inter-nucleosomal contacts between tetranucleosomal structural units through the acidic patches of adjacent nucleosomes.
source: Our previous cryo-EM structure of 30-nm chromatin fiber reveals that N-terminal tails of histone H4 are involved in inter-nucleosomal contacts between the tetranucleosomal structural units through the acidic patches of adjacent nucleosomes (Song et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on a previous cryo-EM structure study by the authors.

claim: IE1 binding may interfere with proper folding of the 30-nm chromatin fiber.
source: Since IE1-CTD is bound at the acidic patch, it is conceivable that IE1 binding may interfere with proper folding of the 30-nm chromatin fiber.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the structural observation and knowledge of H4 tail-acidic patch interactions.
